The '''Solaran Historical Society''' was a historical and archival organization associated with the study of Solaran writing systems, language history, and cultural memory.

== Source Role ==

Source material cites the society in 1905 for a study titled "A Century of Solaran Writing Systems." This places the society in the early twentieth-century conversation around [[Solaran Alphabet|Sunline]], [[Solra]], and the historical legitimacy of the 1895-1898 literacy reforms.

== Work ==

The society likely collected older texts, studied script evolution, preserved educational records, and helped frame the Sunline reform as part of a longer Solaran history rather than a sudden rupture.

Its work complemented the [[Solaran Academy of Linguistics]], which focused more directly on language structure and script development.

== Canon Notes ==

The source does not provide a founding date or full institutional history. This draft uses the 1905 reference as the earliest attested point and leaves continuity after that date open.
